messages.author: bbc31ed8de91caa0
messages.subject: Partial observation set in INLA
parts:
Hi! 

I'm trying to fit an INLA model to coral species data for the purposes of predicting samplign sites for an ROV. We have covariate data including depth, terrain roughness, and habitat type, which we observed with an ROV running a lawnmower pattern over the reef over an area roughly 50m x 50m. Our observations of a specific coral species were taken over a subset of this area, roughly 10m x 10m. Within our 10x10, there is a hotspot of coral species, and anecdotally we know there another hotspot elsewhere on our 50x50m reef, and want to use INLA to estimate the effect of the different covariates on this hotspot, and predict where the second is based on the covariate data. 

I'm modelling these coral observations as a log Cox Gaussian Process, with a matern spatial effect and using the depth, terrain roughness and habitat type as covariates. Our data is gridded, so I was using the approach in https://becarioprecario.bitbucket.io/inla-gitbook/ch-spatial.html section 7.2.1, with a matern kernel for the random spatial effect. 

Is there a way to build into the INLA model areas where observations haven't been taken? Can you indicate that a given grid cell contains covariate data but not observation data, and then predict the response for that grid cell? My initial thought was to simply set the response variable at that grid cell to NA, but I'm getting extremely poor results.

I'm fairly new to INLA, so any help you could give would be greatly appreciated!

Jess

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Partial observation set in INLA
parts:
Hi,
Yes, in principle setting the “unobserved” values to NA should give you the model results for this. However, it sounds like there might not be enough information to do a good prediction of that second hotspot; the random field part won’t know it’s there, so the model has to rely on the covariates only.
Finn

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Partial observation set in INLA
parts:
Hi,
Yes, this works in the same way with SPDE/mesh models, and with inlabru. But with inlabru we’d normally not include the prediction data as NA, but instead just make sure that the mesh covers that region, and the use generate() or predict() for posterior samples/summaries.
Finn
